results_numeric.quantity: Significance of mean offset in L'CO/<L'CO,MS>

evidence.quote: is significant at the $13\sigma$ level

findings_qualitative.value: CO emission is spatially offset from UV, co-spatial with IRAC stellar mass

evidence.quote: the centroid of the CO emission was always co-spatial with the stellar mass distribution as traced by the $Spitzer$/IRAC 3.6 - 8 $\mu$m bands

claims.hypothesis: Starbursts have lower L'CO/LIR than MS galaxies
claims.experiment: CO(2-1) in 12 starbursts vs the Sargent2014 comparison sample
claims.result: Offset to lower L'CO; KS probability 0.07%, 13 sigma mean difference
claims.finding: CO decline is continuous with distance above MS

evidence.quote: we argue that this decline is continuous in these parameters

claims.hypothesis: Starburst boost is due to higher SFE rather than gas fraction
claims.result: Gas fractions similar to MS; depletion times 40-100 Myr
claims.finding: SFE increases continuously; depends on alpha_CO

evidence.quote: the gas fractions remain comparable to those of MS galaxies

why_this_method.value: Select by sSFR rather than SFR to avoid massive MS galaxies

evidence.quote: By selecting galaxies based on their sSFR (cite: Rodighiero2011), we avoid the inclusion of star-forming galaxies at the massive end of the MS

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: alpha_CO=4.36 as alternative; PACS-472 removed due to misidentified redshift

evidence.quote: This misidentification explains a lack of a CO detection at the expected observed frequency thus we remove it from the sample.

limitations_admitted.value: alpha_CO is the dominant systematic uncertainty

evidence.quote: the uncertainty on the appropriate value of $\alpha_{CO}$ is the dominant systematic error in our measure of derived properties
